channel.title: The Retreat Register — Updates
channel.description: Verification progress from The Retreat Register, published with real numbers: coverage snapshots, data findings, and what gets cut from the register and why.

item.title: How to Find the Hidden Costs Before They Disrupt Your Retreat
item.description: The bill that lands after the retreat is the one nobody budgeted. Here's where the ambush hides, line by line.

item.title: Our entire marketing plan is one email
item.description: No drip campaigns, no countdown timers, no 'last chance.' One email when the register opens — and why that's the whole strategy.

item.title: "Quote only" is a feature, not a failure
item.description: The register labels missing prices honestly instead of estimating. Here's why a made-up number is worse than a gap.

item.title: North Carolina: mountains, coast, and the quiet retreat powerhouse between
item.description: From Blue Ridge lodges to coastal estates, North Carolina holds one of the register's most versatile retreat inventories.

item.title: Venue owners: what claiming your listing will (and won't) get you
item.description: Claiming is free and opens at launch. Here's exactly what it changes — and the one thing it will never buy.

item.title: Colorado: the register's mountain workhorse
item.description: Colorado runs deep in the register — and not just the famous ski towns. What planners should know about the state's retreat inventory.

item.title: Book retreats through a platform? Know who pays the middleman
item.description: Commission models hide inside group quotes. Use platforms to browse, then go direct. The register lists the direct lines.

item.title: Wellness retreat venues for teams: real programs, not a fruit plate
item.description: Company wellness offsites are booming while the word wellness means less every year. How the register flags venues actually built for it.

item.title: Yoga retreat venues: the checklist before you book the pretty studio
item.description: Light sells photos; floors, quiet, and schedule freedom run yoga retreats. The unglamorous questions that separate venues.

item.title: Retreat centers near me is the wrong search for groups
item.description: Near me finds what is close to your couch. Groups need airport math. How to use the register's market pages to search like a planner.

item.title: What does retreat mean when you are planning a real trip?
item.description: People search the definition before they search the venue. Here is the practical meaning: lodging, quiet, purpose, and enough structure to make the time away work.

item.title: Trauma-informed retreats: what the label should mean before you trust it
item.description: A rising category with real stakes. The design choices that make a venue genuinely trauma-informed — and the line no retreat should ever claim to cross.

item.title: Reading retreats: the introvert economy stops apologizing
item.description: A weekend where the only agenda item is a book. Why the quietest retreat format on the list is suddenly a format at all.

item.title: Digital-detox retreats: what phone-free actually means at a venue
item.description: The anti-tech mood is not a phase. What separates a real phone-free retreat from a resort with a polite suggestion — policy by policy.

item.title: Dark-sky retreats: darkness is the amenity now
item.description: Certified dark-sky zones, cabins built around the night sky, and why the best amenity at a growing number of venues is what you can't see.

item.title: The nervous-system reset retreat: the product is subtraction
item.description: No workshops, no icebreakers, no agenda. One of the year's rising retreat formats does less on purpose — here's how to spot a real one.

item.title: Couples retreat venues: the real kind, not the movie
item.description: The fastest-growing retreat segment in BookRetreats' industry survey is two people and a cabin. What actually separates a couples-ready venue from a resort with a nice brochure.

item.title: Retreat planning when the travel warnings are loud
item.description: Advisories are spiking searches this week. A quiet fact: a retreat you can drive to skips the country-advisory question entirely. The case for staying domestic.

item.title: Corporate retreat venues: how to shortlist without losing a week
item.description: Company retreat planning starts with a venue shortlist. Here is the four-ask pass that replaces a week of tabs and unanswered forms.

item.title: Why venue capacity numbers are missing everywhere — including here
item.description: Capacity looks like a simple number. It isn't — and pretending otherwise is how planners end up with 60 people and seating for 45.
